summary:
I stated the slit's mouth throughout the SPEC as a designer decision under O10, fixed the minors, and read §0.5, §5's promise and §17.1 as a whole. No module's behaviour changed (only comments in Edge, Factors, Invariance.spec and Perf.spec). Nothing was re-blessed: no value moved.

**G1, the mouth.** Every figure from V2's slant, slantfixed and slantedge scripts reproduces on fixer F's tree to the printed digit.
- I built a scratch closure that is exact on flat faces (var/close1) to separate the mouth from the pieces' grids.
  - F5's blade turned 45° and split 0.0119 apart plays 0.2068 Hard; closed, it plays 0.1833 Normal. So the mouth is worth 0.0235 and the tier.
  - The rest of the gap from the whole blade's 0.1497 is O11's grids (the same split flush plays 0.1725).
  - At 30° no Thinness probe's line crosses a mouth on F5's split blade or on three and four plates. Their drift (0.0016, 0.0073, 0.0075) is the plates' grids, not mouths: fixer F's text and V2's said mouths, and I corrected it. The 3-seam laminate does cross mouths, alike at both gaps.
  - Only the edge sees the mouth at 30°: the raster columns at x ±0.0687 read 0.0278 against 0.0360.
  - V2's 'gap share about 0.04' is 0.024 against the closure.
- O10 now has (i) as built, (ii) a closure and (iii) O11's grid.
  - (ii): an exact closure needs the gap's lateral bound per chord end: the face's own extent and the hiders' union at the probe's depth. Its end tests alone cost ×1.198 on worst valid 8, about 66 ms projected, past the 60 ms guard, so it is not cheap and not adopted.
  - (ii) on the plausible set: it reaches 203 designs and would move d on 96 and the tier on 2 (ribbed bars, Hard → Normal).
  - (ii), dilation form: described, not built.
  - (iii) closes mouths only if its lines read the solid's outline with the hidden gaps filled, which needs the same bound. I wrote that condition rather than the plain claim.
- Every 'at any angle' and 'however slantwise' now reads 'from one part to the next', with the mouth named.
- Fixer D's notes blamed F5's tip for the 45° rise; corrected.

**G2, the minors.**
- The TIE boundary is stated in §5's promise, §5.2, §5.6's Y/Z row, Factors' header, O11, §0.5 and two §17.2 rows: 26 of 120 Y shifts, ΔG 0.0007.
- §5.6 now gives 0.0016 for the turned laminate and 0.0026 for the diagonal. The diagonal's drift is its outline thickening.
- The face-tie count is 839 (reproduced with V2's tools); 853 and 53 still hold for the whole round.
- Golden sizes 42,408 / 84,793 / 24,405; P5 has 237 checkpoints.
- The slowest valid design projects to about 55 ms, about 5 under the guard: 54.7–55.1 from my alternating runs against fix round 1's tree, 53.6–54.3 from fixer F's. Updated in O7, §16.32, §17.2 (both rows), §14.11, §4.9, §5.6 and §16.10.
- T-PERF-01's runs under load are recorded. README is unchanged and still says verify is not green.

**G3.** There are 92 Decision-to-confirm marks, each with its Q or O number apart from the conventions line itself. Every exception is named at the promise with its O-number, and each O row says what the build does and what each option costs. All SPEC and evidence tables keep their column counts.

**Verify:** exit 1, 743 pass and 1 fail. Only T-PERF-01 failed (worst valid 5 at 63.89 ms), with the machine 24–79 % busy. Nothing committed; docs.rar untouched.

deviations: G1 (ii): the lead asked for the closure to be described, and measured only if exact and cheap. I built it anyway, as a measuring tool (var/close1, exact on flat faces), to separate the mouth's share from the pieces' grids, and costed its floor (var/close0). It is not cheap (×1.198 on worst valid 8), so it appears in O10 as an option with those figures, not as a proposal.

G1 (iii): the lead said to name O11's grid as what would close the mouth, re-cuts and seams together. A grid of probes alone still sends a line through a mouth out of the parts. The text therefore says the grid closes the re-cuts and their seams, and closes mouths only where its lines read the solid's outline with the hidden gaps filled, which needs the same lateral bound as (ii).

Attribution: V2's 'the gap's own share about 0.04' (two plates at 45° against their outline's solid) measures 0.024 against the closure; the rest was the solid's own grid changing with its thickness. Fixer F's and V2's 'the gaps' mouths' for the three/four plates' 0.0073/0.0075 is the plates' grids. I corrected the SPEC, the Invariance.spec comments and F's M3-notes. At 30° only the edge sees the mouth.
G2 projection: I quote 'about 55 ms, about 5 under the guard'. My direct runs against fix round 1's tree give 54.7–55.1; fixer F's chain gave 53.6–54.3.

Beyond the listed sections: §4.9 (case count; O7's figures), §5.5's introduction, §5.6's CPU and Y/Z rows, §16.10's VERDICT_WORK_MAX row, §17.2's ties, 2 % rule, invisible-construction and verdict-cost rows, the Invariance.spec and Perf.spec comments, fixer F's three-plate note, and fixer D's '52' (53 by V2's fcmp).
openIssues: For the lead: O10's mouth is a [Decision to confirm]. The default is as built: a tier on F5's blade turned 45° and split; at 30° only the edge's rim columns. An exact closure needs the gap's lateral bound per chord end; its end tests alone cost ×1.198 on the slowest design (about 66 ms, past ANALYSIS_LUNE_MAX_MS); it would move 96 plausible designs, 2 a tier (ribbed bars, Hard → Normal). The mouth belongs to the same family as O11's re-cuts (sampled lines through parts are not the solid's outline), which is the structural question the convergence rule takes to the designer.

For the lead: the mouth also exists outside laminates. A face hidden by a neighbour beside the line ends a chord the same way. Of 33,389 plausible designs, 203 have such ends (130 ribbed bars, 51 wedges in guards). Today's figures include them.

T-PERF-01 has not run on a quiet machine on this tree. verify failed only on timing (worst valid 5 at 63.89 ms, 24–79 % busy), and T-PERF-01 alone failed on F4's stretch (0.398 ms, 24–65 %). The lead's quiet verify and S-PAR-02's Studio runs are still needed before the commit; the digest did not move this round.
My scratch m3-fix3g (scripts, var/close0, var/close1, outputs) is in Temp and loses week-old files. The numbers are in M3-notes and E-S2.13.
